nodes.title: Irreducibility over the quadratic field
nodes.statement: Let f,N,p,λ,K,V be as in the common conventions. If the residual representation is irreducible over G_ℚ and ramified at an odd q|N which is inert or ramified in K, its restriction to G_K is irreducible.
hypotheses: f is a normalized weight-two newform with trivial nebentypus, squarefree level N and Hecke field M; A_f is its modular abelian variety, d=[M:ℚ]=dim A_f. Fix p≥5, λ|p, L=M_λ (or a finite extension), O its integers, and the geometric Tate realization V=V_p(A_f)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L with a stable lattice T. K is imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D, with p=𝔭𝔭̄ and 2 split.
At q||N the residual inertia is nontrivial unipotent; p is odd.
proofSteps: Use local-global compatibility at the squarefree bad prime to obtain a nontrivial residual unipotent τ.
τ² belongs to G_K and remains nontrivial in odd characteristic. A G_K-invariant line must therefore be its unique fixed line.
Normality of G_K makes that unique line G_ℚ-stable, contradicting irreducibility.
acceptance: Retain ramification at q; irreducibility over an index-two subgroup does not follow from global irreducibility alone.
The conclusion is restriction to G_K, correcting the omitted restriction in the printed contradiction.

nodes.title: The two admissible Heegner geometries
nodes.statement: Assume the common conventions, w(f/K)=−1, a residual ramified odd prime nonsplit in K, and the ramified-level condition: if gcd(D,N)>1, every q|gcd(D,N) has local type St twisted by the unramified quadratic character and every q|N/gcd(D,N) splits. Then either Case I holds (all q|N split or ramify), or Case II holds (gcd(D,N)=1 and N=N⁺N⁻, with N⁻ the product of a nonempty even number of inert primes and all q|N⁺ split).
hypotheses: f is a normalized weight-two newform with trivial nebentypus, squarefree level N and Hecke field M; A_f is its modular abelian variety, d=[M:ℚ]=dim A_f. Fix p≥5, λ|p, L=M_λ (or a finite extension), O its integers, and the geometric Tate realization V=V_p(A_f)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L with a stable lattice T. K is imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D, with p=𝔭𝔭̄ and 2 split.
The ramified-level condition is conditional on gcd(D,N)>1; for coprime D it imposes no splitting condition.
proofSteps: Apply the imported local epsilon-factor dictionary, with the archimedean contribution included.
If a level prime ramifies, the stated condition gives Case I. Otherwise the global sign makes the number of inert level primes even.
The residual nonsplit prime makes the inert set nonempty when there is no ramification. Export the corresponding modular or indefinite quaternionic CM-point input.
acceptance: The coprime case with two inert primes is admitted.
A ramified Steinberg prime without the unramified quadratic twist is rejected in Case I.
N⁻ has even cardinality, not odd.

nodes.title: The normalized f-Heegner point
nodes.statement: In Case I or II, import the CM divisor D_K on the appropriate curve X, its Jacobian J, a Hecke-equivariant quotient φ:J→A_f and the coefficient projector ε_f. For an auxiliary prime ℓ away from pND set D_K,ℓ=(T_ℓ−1−ℓ)D_K and Q_K(f)=ε_f[D_K,ℓ]/(a_ℓ(f)−1−ℓ) in J(K)⊗M; put P_K(f)=φQ_K(f). Writing ξ for the degree-one rational Hodge class, set Q_K^ξ=[D_K−deg(D_K)ξ] in J(K)⊗ℚ. Then Q_K(f)=ε_f Q_K^ξ is independent of ℓ; in the modular case the cusp-normalized divisor gives the same projection.
hypotheses: f is a normalized weight-two newform with trivial nebentypus, squarefree level N and Hecke field M; A_f is its modular abelian variety, d=[M:ℚ]=dim A_f. Fix p≥5, λ|p, L=M_λ (or a finite extension), O its integers, and the geometric Tate realization V=V_p(A_f)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L with a stable lattice T. K is imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D, with p=𝔭𝔭̄ and 2 split.
The Hecke idempotent selects the chosen coefficient embedding, rather than merely the rational Galois orbit. The quotient, CM descent and normalized degree-one Hodge class are supplier objects.
proofSteps: The degree of T_ℓ is 1+ℓ, so D_K,ℓ has degree zero. The Weil bound gives |a_ℓ|≤2√ℓ<1+ℓ at every complex embedding, hence the denominator is nonzero.
Project the Hecke relation to the f-component. Eisenstein and cusp corrections vanish under that projector.
Compare with the rational Hodge-divisor representative before coefficient projection; preserve that actual rational point for the eigenlogarithm theorem.
acceptance: The point used in the complex and p-adic formulas is this same P_K(f).
No assertion φε_f=φ is made for the coefficient idempotent.

nodes.statement: For a field L, finite-dimensional L-vector space S, an L-vector space P and an actual linear map loc:S→P, RankOneLocalization(loc) means dim_L S=1 and loc is injective. For Skinner B(e), S=H¹_f(K,V), P=∏_(v|p)H¹_f(K_v,V), and loc is the restriction map with its finite-condition codomain.
hypotheses: S and P are actual vector spaces, not formal fields representing unconstructed Selmer groups.
Finite dimensionality of S is explicit; the arithmetic specialization requires the canonical Bloch–Kato carrier and restriction map.
proofSteps: Use Module.finrank and ordinary injectivity; no new cohomology carrier is introduced.
Expose the equivalent zero-kernel condition on the same map.
Transport along linear equivalences on source and target, keeping loc in the commuting square.
acceptance: The identity on ℚ satisfies the criterion; the zero map on ℚ and the identity on the zero vector space fail it.

nodes.title: Rational Selmer, Kummer and quadratic comparisons
nodes.statement: For A_f, V and K as in the common conventions, identify H¹_f(K,V) with the λ-component of the rational p-adic Selmer group. Kummer gives an injection (A_f(K)⊗ℚ_p)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L→H¹_f(K,V), whose cokernel is the corresponding rational Tate module of Sha[p∞]. At v∤p the rational local finite group is zero; at v|p it is the local rational Kummer image. Restriction identifies H¹_f(K,V) with H¹_f(ℚ,V)⊕H¹_f(ℚ,V⊗χ_D), and conjugation acts by +1 and −1 respectively. Rank and Sha finiteness compare via the quadratic 2-isogeny A_f×A_f^D→Res_(K/ℚ)A_f.
hypotheses: f is a normalized weight-two newform with trivial nebentypus, squarefree level N and Hecke field M; A_f is its modular abelian variety, d=[M:ℚ]=dim A_f. Fix p≥5, λ|p, L=M_λ (or a finite extension), O its integers, and the geometric Tate realization V=V_p(A_f)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L with a stable lattice T. K is imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D, with p=𝔭𝔭̄ and 2 split.
The local and global coefficients retain their continuous topology. Rational statements do not identify finite-level Kummer conditions with raw unramified conditions.
proofSteps: Apply the requested GL₂-type Kummer/Bloch–Kato comparison and finite-generation theorems.
Use p odd and restriction/corestriction to split the quadratic eigenspaces.
Use the requested GL₂-type extension of quadratic point/Sha descent and isogeny invariance; finite 2-primary errors are retained when proving entire Sha finiteness.
acceptance: For M=ℚ this agrees with the existing elliptic Kummer target, not with the pinned explicit 2-Selmer group.
Finite Sha[p∞] kills the rational cokernel but supplies no integral Selmer identification.

nodes.statement: Assume f,N,p,λ,K,V as in the common conventions, p∤N, and rank_ℤ A_f(K)=d with Sha(A_f/K)[p∞] finite. Then dim_L H¹_f(K,V)=1 and each restriction H¹_f(K,V)→H¹_f(K_v,V), v|p, is injective; hence the semilocal map satisfies RankOneLocalization.

nodes.title: The two-dimensional semilocal image
nodes.statement: Assume the common conventions, p∤N, irreducibility of V, self-duality V*≅V(−1), and the associated purity/local vanishing. For S containing the places over pND and infinity, the image of H¹(G_(K,S),V) in H¹(K_𝔭,V)⊕H¹(K_𝔭̄,V) has L-dimension two. Each H¹(K_v,V) has dimension two and each finite subspace H¹_f(K_v,V) has dimension one.
hypotheses: f is a normalized weight-two newform with trivial nebentypus, squarefree level N and Hecke field M; A_f is its modular abelian variety, d=[M:ℚ]=dim A_f. Fix p≥5, λ|p, L=M_λ (or a finite extension), O its integers, and the geometric Tate realization V=V_p(A_f)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L with a stable lattice T. K is imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D, with p=𝔭𝔭̄ and 2 split.
Global and local H⁰ and the dual H⁰ vanish in the indicated realization; local H¹ away from p vanishes rationally.
proofSteps: Use local purity and local Euler characteristics to compute the two local dimensions.
Apply Poitou–Tate with the finite local conditions and their exact annihilators. Identify the dual of the strict kernel with the appropriate global H².
The global Euler characteristic over the imaginary quadratic field gives dim H¹−dim H²=2; subtract the strict kernel to obtain image dimension two.
acceptance: No surjectivity onto the four-dimensional semilocal space is asserted.
Complex places contribute the imaginary-quadratic Euler characteristic.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the strict and one-sided Selmer groups
nodes.statement: Let H=H¹(G_(K,S),V), loc=(loc_𝔭,loc_𝔭̄), H_str=ker(loc), H_𝔭=ker(loc_𝔭) and H_𝔭̄=ker(loc_𝔭̄); these are rational kernels, with no extra away-p conditions. Under the semilocal dimension conclusions and conjugation exchanging the two places, if the image of H¹_f(K,V) under loc has dimension one, then H_𝔭=H_str=H_𝔭̄. If also dim H¹_f(K,V)=1, all three groups vanish. In particular B(e) implies this vanishing.
hypotheses: f is a normalized weight-two newform with trivial nebentypus, squarefree level N and Hecke field M; A_f is its modular abelian variety, d=[M:ℚ]=dim A_f. Fix p≥5, λ|p, L=M_λ (or a finite extension), O its integers, and the geometric Tate realization V=V_p(A_f)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L with a stable lattice T. K is imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D, with p=𝔭𝔭̄ and 2 split.
The finite subspace is loc⁻¹(H¹_f(K_𝔭,V)⊕H¹_f(K_𝔭̄,V)); conjugation exchanges the two local finite lines as well as the full cohomology spaces.
proofSteps: If the two-dimensional semilocal image contained a nonzero vector on one coordinate axis, conjugation would give a nonzero vector on the other. Those vectors span the image.

Its intersection with the product of the two finite lines would then have dimension zero or two, contradicting the assumed dimension one. Thus neither coordinate-axis intersection is nonzero, giving equality of kernels.
The strict kernel lies inside H¹_f(K,V). A one-dimensional finite Selmer group with one-dimensional image has zero kernel.
acceptance: B(e) concerns the product of the two finite local spaces; individual injectivity is a conclusion.
The abstract Lean milestone uses the same submodules and conjugation symmetry, rather than assuming equality of kernels.

nodes.title: The anticyclotomic strict Selmer deformation
nodes.statement: Let K_∞/K be the anticyclotomic ℤ_p-extension, Γ=Gal(K_∞/K), Λ=O[[Γ]], Ψ:G_K→Γ⊂Λ× the tautological character and Λ*=Hom_cts(Λ,ℚ_p/ℤ_p). Form M_∞=T⊗_OΛ* with inverse Ψ-action, and Sel_∞=ker[H¹(G_(K,S),M_∞)→H¹(I_𝔭,M_∞)], with relaxed condition at 𝔭̄ and at the other places of S. Let X_∞ be its compact Pontryagin dual. At a generator γ of Γ, M_∞[γ−1]=W=V/T. Define Sel_𝔭(W) by the identical inertia condition and X_𝔭 its dual. The characteristic ideal is zero for nontorsion X_∞.
hypotheses: f is a normalized weight-two newform with trivial nebentypus, squarefree level N and Hecke field M; A_f is its modular abelian variety, d=[M:ℚ]=dim A_f. Fix p≥5, λ|p, L=M_λ (or a finite extension), O its integers, and the geometric Tate realization V=V_p(A_f)⊗_(M⊗ℚ_p)L with a stable lattice T. K is imaginary quadratic of odd discriminant D, with p=𝔭𝔭̄ and 2 split.

Use the canonical completed group ring, induced continuous representation, local-condition kernels and Pontryagin dual from the suppliers. The condition is restriction to inertia at the chosen 𝔭, not the Bloch–Kato condition.

Fix an O-linear identification Hom_cts(O,ℚ_p/ℤ_p)≅L/O, equivalently a generator of the inverse different, when identifying the Pontryagin augmentation fibre with W=V/T. This coefficient-duality choice is not asserted canonical.
proofSteps: Instantiate the supplied completed-action and inverse-character construction on T.
Use SelmerIwasawaCohomology local conditions for the stated imprimitive kernel and its compact dual; prove finite generation in this arithmetic instance.
Identify the augmentation fibre with W, including the action convention, and use the supplied characteristic-divisor convention.

At an arithmetic ψ of weights (−n,n), n>0, the induced representation has weights n,n−1 at 𝔭 and −n,−n−1 at 𝔭̄. Its negative-weight subspace has dimension two, equal to the +1 complex-conjugation eigenspace; this checks the imported Panchishkin convention without assuming the main conjecture.
